title: My solo browser auto-battler: merge banners, place your army, watch the battle unfold
author: DistributionWise5817
selftext:
Wimpelzug is a medieval fantasy auto-battler you can play for free in the browser, on desktop and mobile.



Buy banners of soldiers, merge three identical ones into a stronger one, place them on the field – then the battle plays out on its own. Terrain like forests, lakes and mountains changes how fights go, and each campaign ends with a boss.



Play: [https://wimpelwerk.itch.io/wimpelzug](https://wimpelwerk.itch.io/wimpelzug)



Feedback very welcome, especially on the first few minutes!

How I built it (workflow):

\- I'm a teacher, not a professional dev. I designed the game (rules, factions, balancing ideas) and worked with Claude as my programmer: I describe what I want, Claude writes and changes the code, and I playtest and give feedback.

\- Everything runs as a single HTML/JavaScript file – map, battlefield, units, effects and even the music and sounds are drawn/generated in code, no game engine.

\- Balancing was done with automated simulations: Claude runs hundreds of bot battles per change and we adjust numbers until win rates look right.

\- The unit portraits were generated with ChatGPT, faction by faction, then cleaned up and placed into the game.

\- Biggest lessons: AI is great at fast iteration, but you have to playtest everything yourself – it confidently produces things that look fine in code and feel wrong in the game.

AI disclosure: This game was made with heavy AI assistance. The code (including the map/battle graphics and sounds) was written together with Claude, and the unit portraits were generated with ChatGPT. Game design, ideas, testing and balancing decisions are mine.

comments.author: qing-turn
comments.body: Merging three identical banners into a stronger one is such a satisfying loop. I'm making a cat tower defense where 10 of the same cat merge into a Giant Cat, and the hardest part for me was making the merge moment feel big enough. How do you show the merge happening? Flash, sound, a short pause?

replies.author: DistributionWise5817
replies.body:
Thanks! I learned the same thing – the merge was too quiet at first. What I do now:

\- a short rising three-note chime the moment the third banner arrives

\- a golden ring that bursts outward from the banner, with the new stars (★★) popping up big over the battlefield, plus the unit's name

\- the banner itself changes color and gets star pips, so you see the upgrade even after the effect fades



No pause – the shop phase is calm anyway, so the effect has room. For a "Giant Cat" I'd go bigger: a short squash-and-stretch on the cat, a screen-wide flash or a tiny camera bump, and a heavier sound than your normal merges. Ten-into-one deserves a moment!

replies.author: qing-turn
replies.body: This is super useful, thanks! Especially the point about still seeing the upgrade after the effect fades. I'll try the camera bump and a heavier sound for the Giant Cat.
